statement: K4,r9 no-fixed-rank recovery theorem. For every fixed integer R>=4 there exists an odd actual dyadic member j_R of the fixed (k,r)=(4,9) family such that the same member has gamma_m<0 simultaneously for every 3<=m<=R. Equivalently, first-recovery ranks in this family have no uniform finite upper bound. This does not assert one finite member is negative at every rank.
closes: refutes every recovery bound depending only on the fixed pair (k,r)
refutes the uniform pre-rank42 waiting-for-positive-surplus route by taking R=42
supplies an exact stable affine-tail recurrence for the K4,r9 family
dependency_gaps: this theorem does not produce one state negative at every rank
it does not classify arbitrary fixed (k,r) transducers
it does not by itself refute the public antichain statement via a different construction
